At higher temperatures, pollen becomes dry, while at lower temperatures, pollen becomes sterile, both leading to no pollination in flower. For example, in the case of the solanaceous family of plants ( which includes tomatoes, chilly, brinjal, etc.), Day temperatures >30° C could cause flower drop. Similarly, night temperatures >22° C or <11° C could lead to flower drop. Humidity Humidity plays a major role in pollen shedding and its transfer.
